calls.head: The Rangers can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Rangers’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Bruins’ power play is near the top of the league. Discipline matters more than usual for the Rangers tonight.
calls.call: The Bruins’ power play creates at least their usual 8.1 expected goals per 60.

calls.head: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams
calls.body: The Rangers and the Bruins are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
calls.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 117.
calls.nums: Hit score (100 is league average): NY Rangers 125 (1st), Boston 109 (7th)

surprises.head: NY Rangers leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: NY Rangers’s bottom-six forwards played 46% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

surprises.head: A big night for J. Swayman
surprises.body: J. Swayman allowed 0 goals on shots worth 2.0 expected goals, 2.0 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 10 starts over the last three seasons.

story.head: Swayman shuts out the Rangers
paras: Fraser Minten opened the scoring late in the third. Jeremy Swayman stopped all 24 shots.
The chances were closer than the score.
